reason: Selected tool ablations support multi-hop graph navigation for function localization, within Python-focused limits.

candidates.title: Test dependency traversal beyond one hop for localization
candidates.rule: For Python issue localization, compare repository graph traversal over calls, imports and inheritance with one-hop or containment-only exploration, especially at function granularity.
candidates.passage: fixing Hops=1 leads to a moderate decline
candidates.finding: The fine-tuned 7B ablation reports larger function-level degradation when traversal is restricted to one hop. Containment alone only marginally recovers performance after full graph traversal is removed.
candidates.conditions: Graph structure and sparse entity indexing accompany the agent interface; relation-rich traversal is one component.
candidates.limitations: Exact ablation deltas were not available in the inspected excerpt. Primarily Python, model-specific fine-tuning and teacher-generated trajectories limit transfer. Localization recall is not equivalent to repair success.
candidates.validation_test: Compare one-hop, containment-only and relation-rich traversal with fixed model and search budget; measure function-level precision/recall, downstream repairs and index build cost.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
